chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said:
The weapon is placed with us, and protected from it. If it were placed with the most evil of Allah’s creation, he would become the best of them.

My father narrated to me that when he built at al-Thaqafiyyah, and there had been made for him a split in the wall, then the house was furnished. So when it was the morning of his wedding, he cast his gaze and saw opposite him fifteen nails. He was alarmed at that and said to her, “Move aside, for I wish to call my mawālī for a need.” Then he scraped it away, and there was not a single nail among them except that he found its tip turned away from the sword, and nothing from them had reached it.

key_terms.السِّلَاحُ: the weapon entrusted to the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.شَرِّ خَلْقِ اللَّهِ: the most evil of Allah’s creation
key_terms.مَدْفُوعٌ عَنْهُ: protected and warded off from harm
key_terms.مَوْضُوعٌ: placed or deposited in their keeping

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith in al-Kāfī say about the weapon kept with the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the weapon entrusted to the Imams عليهم السلام is divinely protected and signifies a special authority associated with them. It then recounts an incident narrated from the Imam’s father, in which hidden nails were found bent away from a sword, showing that no harm reached it.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Muhammad Bin Hakeem, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘The weapons are placed with us<sup>asws</sup>, defended from. Had these been placed with the most evil creature of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, he would have been the best of them.

My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> has narrated to me<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup>, when he built at Al-Sawafiyya, and it was so that for him<sup>asws</sup> there was a wall which had splits in it, so he<sup>asws</sup> renewed the room. So when it was the morning of his<sup>asws</sup> marriage, he<sup>asws</sup> looked around with his<sup>asws</sup> eyesight, and he<sup>asws</sup> saw fifteen nails sticking out. So he<sup>asws</sup> was anxious at that and said to her (the bride): ‘Transfer, for I<sup>asws</sup> want to invite my<sup>asws</sup> friends regarding a need’. So he<sup>asws</sup> scraped it, and there was no nail from these except that its end was bent from the sword, and nothing from these had arrived to it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Raman from Muhammad ibn al-Hakim from abu Ibrahim (a.s.) who has said the following.
“ The arms are kept with us. They are well protected. Even if they would placed with the worst of the creatures he would a good one of them.

My father stated to me that when he married a lady from al-Thaqif the house was decorated for the wedding. Next morning he found fifteen nails drawn into that wall. He became very anxious about it and asked hid bridegroom to leave the house because he needed the handyman to do some work therein. When he examined the wall he found that all the nails had turned back from the sword and none of them had reached it.”
